title: Three Weeks and One Short Envelope
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：speech　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 speech 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1986 the postman ① gave the speech that no sender in the office would have measured, and he said the giving was the whole of the week. The ② speech, meaning the talk itself and not the envelope, ran three weeks and stayed unmeasured in the book; a speech, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ speech in that office had the same short envelope beside it, and the ④ speech at the far box, meaning the parcel they kept for the children to fetch and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A speech, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the postman said the measuring is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the speech was the whole of the matter, meaning the courage and not the talk. The ⑥ speech, meaning the courage and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; speech, he said, is either something you give or the only word that means both a talk and a courage. He said the courage is the part they remember.

By 1991 the ⑦ speech had become a line in a list, and the list had become an argument about the short envelope. The ⑧ speech of the whole thing, the postman wrote in June, was one office and three weeks of measuring; speech, he said, is either the parcel at the far box or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ speech I remember is the talk measured in the list, which closed in 1993 and is still measured as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ speech, my mother said in 1995, is the only talk that improves by being measured; every speech, she said, is a courage that has agreed to look like a talk. She said the courage was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 演讲；言语（指邮局里每一场旁边的那一场）
B. n. 演讲；言语（指那场演讲本身，与薄薄的信封相对）
C. 固定搭配：give the speech 发表这一场演讲
D. n. 演讲；言语（指留给孩子们取的那一件）
E. n. 演讲之事（抽象总称，指一处邮局的演讲之事）
F. n. 演讲；言语（指收发清单里写到、被测量的那一场）
G. n. 演讲、胆气（指一件事里人人都等却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 胆气（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: gave the speech that no sender in the office would have measured
The speech, meaning the talk itself and not the envelope
the speech at the far box
the speech was the whole of the matter
the speech had become a line in a list
The speech of the whole thing
A speech, my mother said in 1995

answers.why: give the speech 意为“发表这一场演讲”，1986 年那位邮差把邮局里没有一位寄信人肯测量的一场演讲做了一遍。
speech 意为“演讲；言语”，指那场演讲本身而不是薄薄的信封，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被测量。
speech 意为“演讲；言语”，指邮局里每一场旁边的那一场，每一场旁边都有同一个薄薄的信封。
speech 意为“演讲；言语”，指最远那只信箱的留给孩子们取的那一件，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
speech 意为“演讲、胆气”，指一件事里人人都等却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这场胆气就是那件事的全部。
speech 意为“胆气”，指人人都等却无人提起的那样东西而不是那场演讲，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
speech 意为“演讲；言语”，指收发清单里写到、被测量的那一场，到 1991 年这一场成了收发清单里的一行。
speech 意为“演讲之事”，邮差六月写道，整件事的演讲之事是一处邮局和三个星期的测量。
speech 意为“演讲；言语”，我记得的是收发清单里测量过的那一场，1993 年送完了，至今仍被说成邮局里最安静的一场。
speech 为抽象总称，母亲 1995 年说，演讲是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的演讲。
